questions.question: Unless a road traffic sign indicates otherwise, on which side of the roadway must you drive in South Africa?

options.text: Either side if the road is clear

questions.explanation: South Africa drives on the left. Keep left except when overtaking or when a sign or marking directs otherwise.
questions.manualRef: K53 manual — position on the roadway; NRTA rules of the road

questions.question: Unless a sign shows otherwise, what is the general speed limit on a public road in an urban area?
questions.explanation: Regulation 293 sets 60 km/h as the general urban-area limit unless a traffic sign indicates a different limit.
questions.manualRef: National Road Traffic Regulations, reg. 293

questions.question: Unless a sign shows otherwise, what is the general speed limit on a public road outside an urban area that is not a freeway?
questions.explanation: Outside urban areas the general limit is 100 km/h, except on freeways (generally 120 km/h) and except where a sign or a lower class-of-vehicle limit applies.
questions.manualRef: National Road Traffic Regulations, reg. 293

questions.question: Unless a sign shows otherwise, what is the general speed limit on a freeway for a light motor vehicle?
questions.explanation: The general freeway limit is 120 km/h unless a sign indicates otherwise. Some heavier vehicles have a lower statutory maximum.
questions.manualRef: National Road Traffic Regulations, reg. 293

questions.question: In good conditions the K53 following-distance method is to stay at least two seconds behind the vehicle in front.
questions.explanation: K53 teaches the two-second rule in good weather and traffic. Increase the gap in rain, at night, on gravel, or when you are towing or driving a heavy vehicle.
questions.manualRef: K53 manual — following distance

questions.question: For an ordinary driver (not a professional driving permit holder), the legal blood-alcohol limit is:
questions.explanation: NRTA section 65 sets 0,05 grams of alcohol per 100 millilitres of blood for ordinary drivers (breath equivalent 0,24 mg per 1 000 ml).
questions.manualRef: National Road Traffic Act 93 of 1996, s. 65

questions.question: For a driver who holds a professional driving permit, the legal blood-alcohol limit is:

options.text: The same as for ordinary drivers

questions.explanation: Professional driving permit holders are held to the stricter 0,02 g/100 ml blood-alcohol limit (breath equivalent 0,10 mg per 1 000 ml).
questions.manualRef: National Road Traffic Act 93 of 1996, s. 65

questions.question: What must you do at this sign?

options.text: Slow down and proceed if the way looks clear, without stopping
Come to a complete stop, then proceed only when it is safe
Stop only if another vehicle is approaching

questions.explanation: A stop sign (R1) requires a complete stop at the stop line, or before the intersecting roadway if there is no line. Move off only when it is safe.
questions.manualRef: SARTSM regulatory sign R1; K53 — stop sign

questions.question: Which of these is a stop sign?
questions.explanation: The stop sign is the red octagon with the word STOP. Yield is the inverted red triangle; no entry is the red disk with a white bar.
questions.manualRef: SARTSM — regulatory signs R1, R2, R3

questions.question: On a typical manual light motor vehicle, click the service-brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Left foot operates the clutch (left pedal). Right foot operates the service brake (centre) and the accelerator (right). Do not rest your foot on the clutch while driving.
questions.manualRef: K53 manual — vehicle controls (light motor vehicle)

questions.question: Match each sign to what it requires you to do.

options.text: Speed limit sign (red-bordered circle with a number)
Come to a complete stop, then go only when safe
Give way to traffic that has right of way; stop if you must
Do not exceed the speed shown, in kilometres per hour

questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell you what you must or must not do. Stop, yield and speed limit are among the most common.
questions.manualRef: SARTSM regulatory signs; K53 road signs

questions.question: Put the K53 moving-off sequence in the correct order.

options.text: Move off when it is safe

questions.explanation: K53 uses a mirror–signal–blind-spot–manoeuvre pattern so you never move into space you have not observed.
questions.manualRef: K53 manual — moving off

questions.question: Unless a sign indicates otherwise, the general speed limit in an urban area is ____ km/h.
questions.explanation: Urban general limit: 60 km/h. Rural (non-freeway): 100 km/h. Freeway: 120 km/h. Always obey a posted sign if there is one.
questions.manualRef: National Road Traffic Regulations, reg. 293

questions.question: Which of the following are true of a person driving a light motor vehicle on a learner's licence? Select all that apply.

options.text: Red letter L plates must be displayed on the front and rear of the vehicle
A licensed driver for that class of vehicle must sit beside the learner
The learner may carry passengers for reward
The learner may not drive on a freeway at all

questions.explanation: Learners must display L plates and be accompanied in a light motor vehicle. They may not drive for reward. Freeway driving is allowed if the accompanying driver is present and the vehicle is permitted on the freeway.
questions.manualRef: NRTA learner's licence conditions; K53 — learner restrictions

questions.question: When you enter a traffic circle (roundabout) in South Africa, you must:

options.text: Force your way in; traffic already in the circle must stop
Yield to traffic approaching from the right / already in the circle
Always stop, even if the circle is empty

questions.explanation: Give way to vehicles from the right and to traffic already circulating. Travel clockwise around the island (left-hand traffic).
questions.manualRef: K53 manual — traffic circles; rules of the road

questions.question: You may not park a vehicle within what distance of a pedestrian crossing?
questions.explanation: Regulation 305 prohibits parking within 9 metres of a pedestrian crossing, among other no-parking places.
questions.manualRef: National Road Traffic Regulations, reg. 305

questions.question: You may not park a vehicle within what distance of an intersection?
questions.explanation: Do not park within 5 metres of an intersection. This keeps sight lines and turning space clear.
questions.manualRef: National Road Traffic Regulations, reg. 305

questions.question: You may cross a solid white barrier line to overtake if no oncoming traffic is visible.
questions.explanation: A solid barrier line must not be crossed. Overtake only where a broken line on your side permits it, and only when it is safe.
questions.manualRef: K53 — road markings; SARTSM barrier lines

questions.question: When must you use your vehicle's headlights?

options.text: Only on a freeway at night
From sunset to sunrise, and at any other time when persons or vehicles are not clearly visible

questions.explanation: Headlamps are required between sunset and sunrise and whenever visibility is poor (fog, smoke, heavy rain, unlit roads).
questions.manualRef: National Road Traffic Regulations — lamps and lighting

questions.question: On a typical manual light motor vehicle, which foot operates the clutch pedal?
questions.explanation: Clutch: left foot. Service brake and accelerator: right foot. Keep the left foot clear of the clutch except when changing gear or moving off.
questions.manualRef: K53 manual — vehicle controls

questions.question: A steady amber (yellow) traffic signal means you must:

options.text: Speed up to beat the red
Stop before the stop line unless you are so close that stopping suddenly would be unsafe
Treat it the same as a green light

questions.explanation: Amber warns that red is next. Stop if you can do so safely. If you are already too close, continue with care — do not accelerate to 'make it'.
questions.manualRef: K53 — traffic signals

questions.question: If your vehicle is stationary on the roadway because of a breakdown, a warning triangle must be placed at least how far behind it?
questions.explanation: Place a red emergency warning triangle at least 45 metres behind the vehicle, on the same side of the road, where approaching drivers can see it.
questions.manualRef: K53 / NRTR — breakdowns and warning triangles

questions.question: Which sign means you must give way (yield) to other traffic?
questions.explanation: Yield is the inverted red triangle with a white centre. Slow down, be ready to stop, and go only when the way is clear.
questions.manualRef: SARTSM regulatory sign R2

questions.question: Click the stop sign in this road scene.
questions.explanation: The octagonal STOP sign is on the right. The inverted triangle on the left is a yield sign — different instruction, different shape.
questions.manualRef: SARTSM — R1 stop and R2 yield

questions.question: Match each control to its job on a manual light motor vehicle.

options.text: Slow or stop the vehicle while moving
Hold the vehicle stationary when parked or waiting

questions.explanation: Use the foot brake to slow while moving. Apply the parking brake when the vehicle must stay put, then release it as you move off.
questions.manualRef: K53 manual — vehicle controls

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is approaching from behind with siren and lights on. Put the correct actions in order.

options.text: Check mirrors and be sure of surrounding traffic
Signal and move as far left as is safe
Resume your position when it is safe

questions.explanation: Give way without creating a new hazard. Do not brake slam in the path of the emergency vehicle, and do not follow it through a red signal.
questions.manualRef: K53 — emergency vehicles

questions.question: The legal minimum tyre tread depth over the complete breadth of the tread is ____ millimetre(s).
questions.explanation: Pneumatic tyres must have at least 1 mm of tread pattern depth across the full breadth. Bald tyres are illegal and unsafe.
questions.manualRef: National Road Traffic Regulations, reg. 212

questions.question: You must dip (dim) your headlights when: (select all that apply)

options.text: You are following closely behind another vehicle
You want to overtake at night on an unlit rural road and need main beam until you are alongside
A police officer has told you never to use headlights in town

questions.explanation: Dip for oncoming vehicles and when you are behind another vehicle so you do not dazzle that driver. Use main beam only where it does not inconvenience others.
questions.manualRef: K53 — use of lights; NRTR lamps

questions.question: What is the minimum age to obtain a learner's licence for a light motor vehicle (code 2)?
questions.explanation: Code 2 (light motor vehicle) learner's licences may be issued from 17 years of age. Motorcycle codes have different minimum ages, and code 3 is 18.
questions.manualRef: National Road Traffic Act — learner's licences; K53 intro

questions.question: A motorcycle learner (code 1) on a public road must:

options.text: Wear a properly fastened protective helmet
Carry a passenger if the passenger holds a car licence
Ride without a helmet in an urban area during the day
Use the pavement when traffic is heavy

questions.explanation: Helmets are compulsory for motorcycle riders and passengers. A learner on a motorcycle may not carry a passenger. Riding on the pavement is illegal.
questions.manualRef: NRTA / NRTR — protective helmets; learner motorcycle conditions
